dbe_source.recommendation: Candidates confused the period with the endpoint of the domain, or confused amplitude with period. Period is a single value derived from the coefficient of x.

lesson.concept: The period of a trig graph is a single number, not an interval and not the endpoint of the given domain. For sin(bx) and cos(bx), period = 360/b. For tan(bx), period = 180/b.
lesson.why: Candidates often give the endpoint of the interval (135, 180, 360) instead of computing the period. The examiner wants the number, not the domain.

example.problem: State the period of y = tan 2x for x in [-135; 135].
work: Ignore the interval. It is the domain, not the period.

probe.problem: State the period of y = cos 3x.

learner_message: The period is a single value: 360/b for sin and cos, 180/b for tan. It is not the endpoint of the interval.
